items.title: Centered smooth-plus-sublinear convergence
items.note: centered: the representation F(x) = psi(x) + gamma(x - x_*) is global (hrep), psi is convex and locally C^{1,1} (LocallyC11On U psi) on the open convex U, gamma is finite convex and positively homogeneous of degree one (Homogeneous.PositiveDegreeOne), x_* minimizes F; for every admissible run R (F convex is part of AdmissibleBFGSRun) whose initial sublevel {F <= F(x_0)} is compact and contained in U: F(x_k) -> F(x_*), and x_k -> x_* if x_* is the unique minimizer. The TeX states the containment of the compact initial sublevel in the neighborhood, so the M7 issue of the article abstract does not recur here. Proof: the article Theorem art:centered (representation only on U, which the global one implies); the library proves the same by the route of this proof (centered_values, centered_iterates). Last sentence: centered_local (F finite convex with unique minimizer, representation and regularity only on an open convex U containing x_*): some eps > 0, chosen before the run, gives iterates in U and convergence in value and iterates for every run with F(x_0) <= F(x_*) + eps; this is the article Corollary art:local-centered, proved with the localization lemma (Lemma M:localization). Non-vacuity: mixedRun for centered; for centered_local, u^2+|v| (psi = u^2, gamma = |v|, U = R^2) and basinRun (UnexcitedMetric.run started at F(x_0) = delta), which starts in every basin (example after mixed_local_facts).

The library proof follows this proof: cocoercivity on the compact initial sublevel, the homogeneous secant pairing 0 <= zeta <= b, the subgradient bound G_gamma, the weighted Cauchy-Schwarz bound L R^2 + 2 G_gamma R for every accepted pair (exists_pair_correction_bound, centered_uniform_correction), then the fixed-reference energy bound with a quadratic cumulative correction (compact_objective_tendsto_min_of_quadratic_corrections). The undisplayed claims of lines 15-22 are centered_split_notation (gamma differentiable at the translated endpoints, y = y_psi + y_gamma, t = a + b) and centered_split_bounds (a, b >= 0, ||y_psi||^2 <= L a, xi^2 <= L R^2 a, 0 <= zeta <= b, zeta <= 2 G_gamma R). The coverage theorem centered is derived from the article theorem art:centered (inward-condition route).

Notation in the proof: a, b, xi, zeta (and y_psi, y_gamma) are variables with their defining equations; x' = x_{k+1} - x_* (translation x_* = 0), s = s_k. centered_split_notation states what the notation rests on: gamma is differentiable at x_k - x_* and x_{k+1} - x_* with gradients g - grad psi, so y_gamma is the secant difference of gamma; y_k = y_psi + y_gamma, t_k = a + b and y_k^T x' = xi + zeta.

Standing assumptions: the theorem's hypotheses, a run with compact initial sublevel K contained in U, a radius R (Rad) with ||x - x_*|| <= R on K, L > 0 with the cocoercivity estimate on K, G_gamma bounding all subgradients of gamma (Euclidean norms); for every k. Lean division by zero is 0, which is the convention of the last sentence (and the numerators do vanish).

items.title: Transformed-gauge convergence
items.note: gamma finite convex, Homogeneous.PositiveDegreeOne, coercive (Tendsto gamma (cocompact) atTop); Phi : R -> R constrained on [0, oo): ContinuousOn (Ici 0), ConvexOn (Ici 0), StrictMonoOn (Ici 0), Phi 0 = 0, ContDiffOn R 2 (Ioi 0), deriv Phi r > 0 for r > 0 (the library structure IncreasingTransform, increasingTransform_iff); every admissible run on F(x) = Phi(gamma(x - x_*)) has x_k -> x_*.

The library proves the theorem by the inverse-free annulus route described after the proof (prose/007): a correction bound R_k <= (1+C)^2 Delta_k/((1-c_2)c_1) on every positive band, summable corrections, contradiction with the energy bound, then coercivity and strict increase. The inverse route of the displays is proved separately: transform_inverse (Phi maps [0,oo) bijectively onto itself; the library inverse is unique there), disp/003-006. Undisplayed: compact sublevels (objective_sublevel_compact).

After the translation x_* = 0, x_k is x_k - x_*. a_k (variable) = g_k^T(x_k - x_*) = gamma(x_k - x_*) Phi'(gamma(x_k - x_*)) = Theta(F_k), with Phi^{-1} any inverse of Phi on [0, oo) (Phiinv; it agrees there with the library inverse, transform_inverse) and Theta(t) = Phi^{-1}(t) Phi'(Phi^{-1}(t)) a variable with its defining equation. Stated for every admissible run and every k, without the proof's contradiction hypothesis F_k >= L > 0 for all k (which no run satisfies; the identity does not need it).

For every L > 0 (in the proof, the lower bound of its contradiction hypothesis, not needed here) and every t in [L, F_0] (F_0 = F(x_0)), Theta has derivative 1 + r Phi''(r)/Phi'(r) at t with r = Phi^{-1}(t) (Phi'' = deriv (deriv Phi)), and this expression is bounded on [L, F_0].

y_k^T(x_{k+1} - x_*) = d_k + a_{k+1} - a_k with a_k = g_k^T(x_k - x_*); for every admissible run and every k, without the contradiction hypothesis; it holds for every reference point (the hypotheses on gamma and Phi are unused).

With L > 0 and C >= 0 a Lipschitz constant of Theta on [L, F_0] (supplied by the bounded derivative of disp/004), for every k with F(x_{k+1}) >= L: |a_{k+1} - a_k| <= C Delta_k (the preceding undisplayed claim) and R_k = (y_k^T(x_{k+1}-x_*))^2/t_k <= (1+C)^2/((1-c_2)c_1) Delta_k, via (M:basic). The proof's contradiction hypothesis F_k >= L for all k (which no run satisfies) is weakened to this pointwise one (F(x_k) >= F(x_{k+1}) by monotonicity). Satisfiable: the example after transform_correction_annulus (absRun on |x|, Phi = id, Theta = id, C = 1, k = 0, L = F(x_1) > 0).

Setting of line 67 as hypotheses: m >= 1 pieces l_i(x) = a_i^T x + b_i, p(x) the greatest of the l_i(x) (IsGreatest), psi convex and locally C^{1,1} on R^n, F = psi + p, x_* the unique minimizer; I_* (Finset with defining property) and q(z) = max_{i in I_*} a_i^T z (IsGreatest over I_*) are variables. Conclusion: some Euclidean ball radius eps > 0 with p(x_* + z) = p(x_*) + q(z) for ||z|| < eps. The identity only uses hp (it holds at every point).

For i_0 in I_*, j not in I_*, delta_j (variable) = p(x_*) - l_j(x_*): the identity l_{i_0}(x_*+z) - l_j(x_*+z) = delta_j + (a_{i_0} - a_j)^T z for all z, delta_j > 0, positivity for ||z|| <= delta_j/(2||a_{i_0} - a_j||) when a_{i_0} != a_j (Euclidean norms), and positivity for all z when a_{i_0} = a_j (the parallel case). Non-vacuity: p = max{x, -x, x-1} on R (x_* = 0, I_* = {0, 1}, inactive j = 2, delta_j = 1).
The display defines P_j (variable with the first set as defining equation) and asserts the equality with {x : (a_j - a_i)^T x >= b_i - b_j for all i}; LEAN for the assertion. Uses only hp.

tau_* is the EReal variable tau with defining equation tau = iInf over the inactive indices j of sInf of F over P_j. maxAffine_threshold_def unfolds it: it equals the library threshold (the infimum of F over the union of the inactive P_j); an empty P_j has infimum +oo; with no inactive index tau_* = +oo; otherwise the minimum over the finitely many inactive indices is attained (the "min" of the display).

The library also proves the H_0^{-1}-metric fiber characterization of the limit (projectRun_limit_lift).
The conclusion of lifting.

For an admissible run, a minimizer x_* (F_* = F(x_*)), R_k <= Rbar for all k, S_N and E_0 as variables: for N >= 1 (S_0 = 0) F(x_N) - F_* <= sqrt((E_0 + Rbar N)/S_N) with no further hypothesis (first conjunct, from (M:energybound)); for runs with bounded gradients, sqrt(N) times the bound tends to 0 (o(N^{-1/2})) and S_N/N^2 -> oo (second conjunct). The hypothesis is not automatic (F(x,y) = max{x^2 - y, 0} is convex with minimizers and unbounded gradients on every positive sublevel), but no admissible run violating the literal claim is known.

R_k = (y_k^T x_{k+1})^2/t_k (x_* = 0) <= C_gamma F(x_{k+1}) with C_gamma = max{2, 1 + Lambda/mu} (variable with defining equation).

A_N = E_0 + C_gamma sum_{j=1}^N F(x_j) is the variable A with its defining equation (sum written as sum_{k<N} F(x_{k+1})), E_0 = x_0^T H_0^{-1} x_0. quadGauge_budget: it is the library valueCorrectionBudget 0 C_gamma, A_{N+1} = A_N + C_gamma F(x_{N+1}), F(x_N)^2 S_N <= A_N, A_N >= E_0 > 0.

With a_0 > 0, N_0 such that S_N >= a_0 N^2 for N >= N_0 (prose/034), for every N >= max(N_0, 1): F(x_N) <= sqrt(A_N)/(sqrt(a_0) N) (prose/035), the exact increment identity and the bound C_gamma/(sqrt(a_0) N).
For N >= 1: sqrt(A_N) - sqrt(A_{N-1}) <= C_gamma/sqrt(S_N), and N C_gamma/sqrt(S_N) -> 0 (o(N^{-1})).

For fixed 0 < c_1 < c_2 < 1, A > 0, v_0 > 0, 0 < rho < (1-c_1)/(1+c_1) on F(u,v) = u^2 + |v|: an admissible run with x_0 = (0, v_0), H_0 = diag(A, (1+rho)/(2 rho) v_0), alpha_k = 2 rho exists (UnexcitedMetric.run), and every admissible run with these x_0, H_0 and lengths has x_k = (0, (-rho)^k v_0) and H_k = diag(A, (1+rho)/(2 rho) rho^k v_0) (ordinary BFGS is deterministic once the lengths are fixed).

Standing (lines 189): phi : R -> R convex, bounded below on [0, oo), phi'(0) = a < 0, 0 < c_1 < c_2 < 1, sigma = (c_1+c_2)/2, psi(t) = phi(t) - sigma a t (variables), and M, z with 0 < z < M, z a minimizer of psi on [0, M], psi(z) < psi(0) (which tilted_setup supplies).

items.note: The literature result used by the proof (WW, Theorem 2.5) in the local form used, proved in Lean: on a compact subset of the open set where psi is convex and locally C^{1,1}, ||grad psi(y) - grad psi(x)||^2 <= L (grad psi(y) - grad psi(x))^T (y - x).

items.anchor: It does not require a globally Lipschitz gradient or minimization of each original summand at the center.
items.note: x^4 + |x| on R satisfies every hypothesis of Theorem F:centered (so every run converges) while grad psi(x) = 4x^3 has no global Lipschitz constant; the summands-not-minimized instance is the article one. Non-vacuity: admissible runs on x^4+|x| exist (quarticAbs_run_exists, from AdmissibleRunExistence.exists_admissible_run).

items.note: Five-piece ray: the ray function is differentiable at alpha = 3 (derivative 0) and alpha = 3 passes the scalar Armijo and weak-Wolfe tests, but h is not differentiable at the point.

discrepancies.description: Unresolved source-note labels. companion/chapters/06_F.tex:9 (first paragraph of Section 6.1, before Theorem 6.1 = F:centered; frozen span F.span.1, source bfgs_lean_stage1/master_report/latex/chapters/families.tex:7) prints, on printed page 34 of the built companion (companion/build/master.pdf, PDF page 40): "This module collects the nonredundant structural consequences from [M], [P], [E] and [Q]." The bracketed letters print literally, like citation keys, and resolve to nothing: the companion has no bibliography entry or label [M], [P], [E] or [Q], its chapters are numbered 1 to 14, [P] matches no chapter, and [M], [E], [Q] read as the letters of Chapters 2, 14 and 10, which they do not mean ([Q] in particular is not Chapter 10, Flat contours and parabolic branches). In the sources they are working reports of the research record, cited in the original master report as [SM], [SP], [SE], [SQ] (BFGS_MASTER_REPORT_LaTeX/report/master.tex:130, module F: "Consolidated proofs from [SM], [SP], [SE] and [SQ]"; bibliography.tex:11, 17, 18, 19): [SM] "Full BFGS on mixed smooth--nonsmooth convex objectives" (common principal-minor and fixed-reference energy foundation), [SP] "Local convergence of full BFGS for smooth convex plus polyhedral objectives" (local reduction, certified basin, affine-fiber lifting), [SE] "BFGS after the convex nonsmooth counterexample", Section 3 (increasing smooth transforms of coercive gauges), [SQ] "Next BFGS research directions, with finite-horizon rate corollaries" (rates). editorial/generate_companion.py:29 maps the citation keys SP, SQ, SE to Chapter F itself and SM to Chapter M, but it rewrites only \cite keys, not these bare bracketed letters; "This module" is the source report's term for a chapter (W8 type).
